To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can automatically derive glue code to translate between agents' data structures, and we can do this using a small number of simple rules, and that we need only partial formalizations to get started.

(i) we can derive a program that translates between the two representations, (ii) the program has a small and fixed size, independent of the size of the two representations, and (iii) the program is correct, in the sense that it translates all the information from the source representation to the target representation.
we can get agents to interoperate by solving functional equations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
finding a way to derive glue-code automatically.

the development of a formal theory for the semantics of agent interoperation and the development of a glue code derivation system that uses the formal theory to generate glue code for agent interoperation.
the automatic generation of glue code for interoperation of agents that use heterogeneous knowledge representation languages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the glue-code generation problem has been solved, but that there is still work to be done on finding formalizations of the source and/or target domains.
we have found a way to derive the glue code for interoperation between two agents, given the source and target representations and the formal theories of the semantics of those representations.
the derivation of glue code for agent interoperation is possible, and that the derivation process can be automated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are developing a system for deriving glue code for interoperation of agent systems.
we are developing a theory for deriving glue code for agent interoperation.
we have developed a general approach to interoperation of agents that is based on formal semantic theories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
agent interoperation may be achieved by automatic code generation, without requiring the agents themselves to be aware of the interoperation.
agent communication is not as intractable as it may seem, and that we have a way to get agents to communicate without having to write glue code by hand.
it is possible to derive the glue code that is necessary to interoperate with agents that have different data structures and that the derivation is automatic and can be carried out at run time.
